summary: enable branch coverage and upload xml
pull_request_body: This change enables branch coverage in the coverage gate and keeps the XML report as a CI artifact. Branch coverage is off in [tool.coverage.run]. A guard like `if a or b: raise` counts as covered when one side runs. Setting `branch = true` makes coverage.py measure both sides. CI writes .data/coverage.xml for diff-cover and then discards it. A reviewer cannot see per-file figures without a new run. The Tests & Coverage job now uploads the file as an artifact with a 7-day retention. The fail_under change is dropped per the owner decision on #2356. The 85% floor and 90% changed-line gate stay as they are.
why: #2163 reports that the coverage gate measures only lines, not branches, so a guard like `if a or b: raise` counts as covered when one side runs. CI also discards .data/coverage.xml after diff-cover reads it, so a reviewer cannot see per-file figures without a new run.
what_changes: pyproject.toml sets `branch = true` in [tool.coverage.run] so coverage.py measures both sides of each conditional
.github/workflows/ci.yml adds an upload-artifact step to the Tests & Coverage job that keeps .data/coverage.xml with a 7-day retention
feasibility: Confirmed: pyproject.toml line 229 shows `data_file = ".data/.coverage"` in [tool.coverage.run] with no `branch` key, matching the issue's claim at pyproject.toml:197-202.
Confirmed: .github/workflows/ci.yml has no upload-artifact step for .data/coverage.xml; the job runs diff-cover and ends without keeping the file.

The Tests & Coverage job took 245-307 s in the last 8 runs (284.5 s average). Branch measurement adds time. The 300 s average limit is the hard bound; the PR also reports against the 240 s target from #2356.

First checks the implementation runs: `uv run devops ci test` to verify the suite passes with branch coverage on; `uv run devops ci --check --only lint,format,actionlint,zizmor` to verify the workflow passes actionlint and zizmor.
existing_tool: coverage.py and pytest-cov, which the project already uses, measure branches when `branch = true` is set. `actions/upload-artifact` keeps the report. Nothing is built.

decisions.decision: Set `branch = true` in [tool.coverage.run] rather than passing `--branch` on the command line
decisions.reason: The configuration file is the single source of truth for coverage settings. Both the local gate and CI read it, so one change covers both.
Every other action in ci.yml is pinned by SHA. This matches the existing pattern and prevents a silent version change.
The artifact is for review of a recent run. A short retention keeps storage low while covering the review window.
The owner dropped the fail_under raise from this issue per the decision on #2356. The 85% floor and 90% changed-line gate stay as they are.

rejected.alternative: Raise `fail_under` to the measured total with branches on
rejected.evidence: The owner struck this from the issue on 2026-10-27, deferring it to #2356 which sets a lower global floor of 85% and a gate on changed lines.

rejected.alternative: Build a custom artifact upload script
rejected.evidence: `actions/upload-artifact` already uploads a file by path with a retention period. The project uses it for the SARIF report in the same workflow. Building a custom script adds tokens to build, keep and fix with no benefit.

added.name: branch-coverage-measurement
added.text: The coverage configuration SHALL set `branch = true` in `[tool.coverage.run]` so that coverage.py measures both sides of each conditional.

scenarios.name: branch key present in pyproject
scenarios.when: pyproject.toml is parsed and the [tool.coverage.run] table is read
scenarios.then: the table contains the key `branch` with the value `true`

added.name: coverage-xml-artifact-upload
added.text: The `Tests & Coverage` job SHALL upload `.data/coverage.xml` as a CI artifact with a retention period of at most 14 days.

scenarios.name: upload step in workflow
scenarios.when: the `Tests & Coverage` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml is read
scenarios.then: it contains a step that uses `actions/upload-artifact` with `path` set to `.data/coverage.xml` and a `retention-days` input

groups.title: Enable branch coverage in pyproject.toml
groups.test: Write a test in tests/test_coverage_config.py. The test reads pyproject.toml with tomllib, parses the [tool.coverage.run] table, and asserts that the key `branch` has the value `True`. The test fails before the change because the key is absent
groups.implementation: Add `branch = true` to the [tool.coverage.run] section of pyproject.toml, after the existing `parallel = true` line
groups.verify: uv run devops ci test tests/test_coverage_config.py

groups.title: Upload coverage XML as CI artifact
groups.test: Write a test in tests/test_workflows.py. The test reads .github/workflows/ci.yml with yaml.safe_load, finds the job whose `name` is `Tests & Coverage`, and asserts that one of its steps has `uses` starting with `actions/upload-artifact@` and a `with` table containing `path` set to `.data/coverage.xml` and a `retention-days` key. The test fails before the change because no such step exists
groups.implementation: Add a step after the Changed-Line Coverage step in the Tests & Coverage job: name `Upload Coverage XML`, uses `actions/upload-artifact` pinned by commit SHA, with `name: coverage-xml`, `path: .data/coverage.xml`, and `retention-days: 7`. Add `if: always()` so the artifact uploads even when the gate fails
